findings.description: The check cannot pass against any correct stamper, because its own setup destroys the record under test: `open(p, "w")` is evaluated before the argument expression `open(p).read()`, so the file is truncated to zero bytes and then written with the re.sub of an empty string. The record the whole clause turns on ends up a 0-byte file with no `schema` key, and every conforming implementation reports it as a v1 skip. Worse, the r2 headline string `order-independent` prints anyway, because both orderings skip identically — the third appearance of the pass-string-for-the-wrong-reason failure mode, and this time on the one string that is supposed to prove AC6.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:171-175, the mutation `open(p, "w").write(re.sub(r"^last_confirmed:.*$", "last_confirmed: 2026-01-20", open(p).read(), count=1, flags=re.M))`. Reproduced: copied mixed/_memory/context/atlas-region-topology-mPmy8XBe5H.md (1254 bytes), ran that exact block -> 0 bytes. Ran the whole C-5 check verbatim against a conforming reference stamper I wrote for the audit: output was `skipped: ... (v1 record, no schema key)` / `stamped: 0  skipped: 1`, `order-independent` PRINTED, `grep -c '^stamped: .*atlas-region-topology'` returned 0 (constitution.md:190 requires 1), the closing line read `stamped: 0  skipped: 0` not `stamped: 1  skipped: 0`, and the record never reached `last_confirmed: 2026-02-17`. Re-ran the same check with only the mutation corrected to read-then-write (the form C-4 already uses at constitution.md:139-142): `stamped: ... 2026-01-20 -> 2026-02-17`, `stamped: 1  skipped: 0`, `order-independent`, `grep -c` = 1, record at 2026-02-17. The single change from broken to discriminating is `t = open(p).read()` on its own line.

findings.description: C-3 and C-5 are both blockers and they contradict each other on an input the batch redesign makes ordinary: one record named by two `--note` groups whose dates straddle the record's existing `last_confirmed`. C-3's text says the older group means the record 'is not written', 'is reported as skipped', and is 'byte-identical afterwards'; C-5 case 2 says the record 'takes the latest of the group dates' and 'appears in the output at most once'. No implementation satisfies both, and the constitution never states which rule applies first.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:112 (C-3) 'When a group's note date is earlier than or equal to the record's existing `last_confirmed`, the record is not written. It is reported as skipped with a reason naming both dates, and the file is byte-identical afterwards.' vs constitution.md:162 (C-5 case 2) 'The record takes the **latest** of the group dates' and constitution.md:159 'each distinct record is written at most once and appears in the output at most once'. Constructed the case against the real fixture: atlas-region-topology at last_confirmed 2026-02-10, group A = notes/2025-12-02-atlas-steerco (older), group B = notes/2026-02-17-atlas-freeze-exceptions (newer). Collapse-then-compare (my reference stamper) prints exactly one line, `stamped: ... 2026-02-10 -> 2026-02-17`, no `skipped:` line, and the file changes — violating all three of C-3's assertions. Compare-per-group-then-act prints both a `skipped:` and a `stamped:` for one record, violating C-5's 'at most once'. Veto-on-any-older holds at 2026-02-10, violating C-5's 'takes the latest'. Neither clause's own check reaches the case: C-3's uses two single-group invocations (constitution.md:119-122) and C-5's uses two dates both later than the record's (constitution.md:169-175), so both checks stay green while the texts disagree. This is new in r2 — under r1's per-input scoping one invocation carried one date and the case could not arise.

findings.description: The insertion half carries the identical truncate-before-read bug, and this time the clause's own pass string prints on the wreckage. The record is emptied, a conforming stamper reports it as a v1 skip, `sed -n '1,20p'` prints nothing at all, and `lint-scope.sh` reports `failures: 0` — which is exactly what constitution.md:216 says a pass looks like. The half that exists to catch a key inserted at the wrong contract position is satisfied by a record with no keys.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:204-207, `open(p, "w").write(re.sub(r"^last_confirmed:.*\n", "", open(p).read(), count=1, flags=re.M))`. Reproduced standalone: 1254 bytes -> 0 bytes. Ran the full insertion half against the reference stamper: `skipped: _memory/context/atlas-region-topology-mPmy8XBe5H.md (v1 record, no schema key)`, `sed -n '1,20p'` empty, `bash inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh "$S" | grep -E '^(failures|FAIL)'` -> `failures: 0`. The budget half, by contrast, is now sound and I verified it end to end: the probe scope lints `failures: 0` with the note present (note counted as the scope's one v1 file), a hand-inserted `last_confirmed` closes the block on line 21 and reports `frontmatter-budget: closing --- on line 21, past the 20-line budget` / `failures: 1`, and the reference stamper prints `skipped: ... (frontmatter budget: ... closes --- on line 21, past the 20-line budget)`, `exit=0`, `held`. r1's C-6 defect is genuinely closed; the bug moved to the other half.

findings.description: The r2 claim that batch scope makes the placement 'forced rather than chosen' does not hold, so the r1 minor is not closed — and the clause now requires SKILL.md to ship the unsound reason as prose. Batch scope removes the intra-loop placements, but SKILL.md's phases are not one fused per-input pipeline: each phase runs its own loop over the queue, so the end of phase 3 is a second point at which every `--note` group exists, every note is groomed, and nothing else has happened. A single batch call there is fully admissible, and phase 4 (dispose source) creates no dependency that rules it out.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:505 'That leaves exactly one admissible point — after the phase 2.5 through phase 4 loop has completed for every input in the queue, and before phase 5' and 'SKILL.md states both the placement and the reason it is not a choice'. SKILL.md's actual structure: :24 'Six phases, plus a 2.5 that slots in ahead of grooming'; :41 (phase 2) 'For each file in `_inbox/`, dispatch by extension'; :59 (phase 2.5) 'For each inbox file, in order:'; :83 (phase 3) 'Emit one note per input at `<scope-root>/notes/...`'; :128-134 (phase 4) 'Dispose Source' — text sources deleted, binary sources moved, nothing touching `_memory/` or note dates. Under that structure the grooming loop completes for the whole queue at the end of phase 3, which is outside every per-input loop and before phase 5, so it satisfies every constraint the clause names. The clause text is still literally decidable, so a checker can settle placement; what cannot be met honestly is the requirement to write down why it is not a choice.

findings.description: The batch interface has no defined behavior for the common case, and no clause supplies one. C-1 makes a zero-group invocation a hard error, C-17 locates one unconditional call in the flow, and nothing anywhere says the call is skipped when phase 2.5 found no confirmations — which is most runs. A worker who wires the call as C-17 describes ships a skill that exits nonzero on every clean inbox. The sibling case, a `--note` group with a note and no record paths after it (an input that confirmed nothing while other inputs did), is undefined in the same way: error, or a legal empty group.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:64 'if any named record path or `--note` path does not exist or does not parse, or if no `--note` group is given at all, the script writes nothing, names the path that failed, and exits nonzero'; constitution.md:505 locates the call with no conditionality; constitution.md:44 pins `--dry-run` placement and record-path resolution but says nothing about a group with zero records. C-17's judgment rubric (constitution.md:515) asks 'Could two agents following this document run the stamp at two different points?' and has no clause to settle the zero-confirmation case against. Related and unstated: constitution.md:44 says 'Record paths may be absolute or relative to the scope root' and is silent on how a `--note` path resolves, yet every check in the document (C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, C-6, C-7, C-13's saboteur at :413) passes notes relative to the scope root while the checker's cwd is the repo root — a stamper resolving notes against cwd fails every check for a reason the contract never named. Also unstated: what happens when `--dry-run` appears after the first `--note`.

findings.description: The mechanical half states a pass condition that a correct artifact cannot meet. `Four` must not be gone from EVALS.md: line 12 reads 'Four prior notes, two open-question slugs live in all four' as part of the `unacknowledged-tension` fixture description, and it is about notes, not about the fixture count. A checker following the stated criterion fails a correct edit; a worker following it makes a collateral edit to an unrelated sentence.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:454 '`Four` must be gone'. Ran the clause's grep verbatim: `/usr/bin/grep -n 'Four\|confirmation-writethrough' _maintenance/inbox-to-memory/EVALS.md` returns two hits, `:9` (the fixture count, which must move) and `:12` ('Meridian Freight's Dockside pilot at the Bexley Road terminal. Four prior notes, ...', which must not). The other three assertions of the half are sound and I verified their anchors: `grep -c '^| [0-9]\.'` returns 4 today and matches only the Grading table's rows at :125-128 (the per-scenario tables use `| Expect | Pass condition |`, so nothing pollutes the count); the table spans :123-128 as the clause says; the closing claim is at :130, 'The delta is widest on 1 and 4'.

findings.description: C-3's check is the only one of the four `held`/`untouched` harnesses with no exit assertion, so its pass string prints for a stamper that crashed on both invocations. C-4 and C-6 both guard theirs with `echo "exit=$?"`; C-3 does not, and it is a blocker.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:115-125 — the loop at :119-122 discards each invocation's status and :123 prints `held` on a shasum comparison alone. Compare constitution.md:146 (C-4, `; echo "exit=$?"`) and constitution.md:266 (C-6, same). The prose at :127 does require both runs to print `skipped:`, which is the backstop, but it is prose beside a block whose only machine-readable outcome is `held`.

findings.description: `dry and wet output identical` is satisfied by a stamper that prints nothing at all, so one of C-1's two r2 additions is trivially true in the failure case it most needs to exclude.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:75 `[ "$dry" = "$wet" ] && echo "dry and wet output identical"`. Observed directly during the audit: while my reference stamper was still erroring out on `declare -A` (bash 3.2), both `$dry` and `$wet` were empty and the line printed. The clause's other assertions (the `stamped:` line, `exit=0`, `last_confirmed: 2026-02-17`) do catch it, so this is a soft spot rather than a hole — but it is the same shape as the defect r1 filed against C-6.

findings.description: The order-independence requirement is stated as byte-identical output, which for any run touching more than one record forces a canonical output order the script contract never specifies and the check never exercises. A stamper emitting records in first-encounter order — the obvious implementation, and the only one the contract's 'one line per distinct record' suggests — fails the clause text on a two-record two-group swap while passing the clause's check.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:162 'the run's output is identical whichever order the groups were passed in'; constitution.md:44-50 pins the line formats and the closing count but no ordering. C-5's check uses a single record (constitution.md:168 `R=...atlas-region-topology...`), so the requirement is asserted at the one arity where it is free. Also worth recording: case 1 ('twice inside one `--note` group') is not separately exercised — the single invocation at constitution.md:185 passes `"$R" "$S2/$R"`, which is case 3. It is logically subsumed (no dedupe collapses two distinct strings but not two identical ones), so this is not a hole, but the clause's claim that the check covers three sub-cases is really two.

findings.description: The saboteur is a genuine improvement — I ran it against a conforming stamper and confirmed it delegates byte-for-byte and then additionally stamps only the v1 record, which is exactly what the clause claims. Two residual couplings remain: it resolves `--note` paths as `$root/$a` under `set -euo pipefail`, so an absolute note path anywhere in the new section kills it for a parsing reason rather than a v1 reason; and it stamps by `sed`-inserting before `^source_refs:`, so a v1 record without that key makes the saboteur silently inert and the suite stays green for a reason unrelated to what the check concludes.
findings.evidence: Installed the saboteur from constitution.md:400-422 in a scratch directory over a conforming reference stamper and ran it on a copy of `mixed/`: output was byte-identical to the real run (`skipped: ... (v1 record, no schema key)` / `stamped: ... 2026-02-10 -> 2026-02-17` / `stamped: 1  skipped: 1`, exit 0) and the v1 record gained `last_confirmed: 2026-02-17` at line 7. r1's confound — the stub reddening a suite by changing the output shape — is gone. Under `--dry-run` the saboteur also writes the v1 record (verified: 'DRY-RUN SABOTEUR WROTE V1'), which over-reaches slightly but still reddens for a v1-write reason. The `sed` depends on `mixed/_memory/decisions/freeze-window-owned-by-ops-ocPwdpeY0a.md` carrying `source_refs:`, which it does; any other v1 record the new section builds may not.

findings.description: The migrator's wiring precedent is cited at the wrong line, twice. `require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "scripts/migrate-scope.sh"` is at tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:600, not :599; :599 is `require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "migrate this scope"`. This is the exact defect class C-15 exists to police, in the document that writes C-15.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:25 'the migrator's wiring precedent, which C-17 mirrors, is at `tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:596-602`: `require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "scripts/migrate-scope.sh"` sits at `:599`' and constitution.md:507 'the way the migrator's is pinned at `tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:599`'. Actual: :598 `require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "| migrate  |"`, :599 `require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "migrate this scope"`, :600 `require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "scripts/migrate-scope.sh"`, :601 `require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "references/migration.md"`. The r0 verdict had this right at :600; r1 restated it as :599 and the constitution took the wrong one.

findings.description: The environment section names yq, nanoid, and the shell shadowing, and omits the one environment fact the r2 script contract actually collides with: the only bash on this box is 3.2.57, which has no associative arrays. Batch scope makes the stamper the first script in this repo that needs a keyed map (record realpath -> latest group date, per C-5 case 2), and the natural `declare -A` implementation dies at parse time.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:22-30 lists tool paths and the grep/find/cat shadowing but no bash version. `bash --version` -> 'GNU bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin23)'; `command -v bash` -> /bin/bash; no homebrew bash present. Hit this directly while writing the reference stamper: `declare: -A: invalid option` at every invocation, followed by `order[@]: unbound variable`. Every script in the repo uses `#!/usr/bin/env bash` and every check in the constitution invokes `bash <script>`, so 3.2 is what the deliverable will run under.

findings.description: The floor of twelve re-derives correctly and the new document-level obligation on `_memory.template.md` is the right shape, but the sweep surfaces one sibling the floor does not name and the clause's framing does not reach: `assets/claude-md/journal.template.md:23` lists `last_confirmed: YYYY-MM-DD` as required frontmatter with no account of how the value is set, exactly parallel to the `:21` hit that earned `_memory.template.md` its obligation. Question 1 arguably answers no for journal scope (there is no `_memory/` there), which is why I file this as an observation rather than a defect — but a checker re-deriving the sweep will hit it and has no ruling to lean on.
findings.evidence: Ran the sweep at constitution.md:341-342 verbatim. All twelve floor locations resolve: SKILL.md:26, :138, :168, :361, :455; README.md:74; assets/claude-md/_memory.template.md:21 (`last_confirmed: YYYY-MM-DD` inside the required-frontmatter block), :65; client.template.md:71; project.template.md:55; references/migration.md:37; references/retrieval-funnel.md:40. The migrate-scope.sh citation is correct: :348-349 is the comment 'A record nobody has re-confirmed was last confirmed the day it was written. / Any later date would assert a review that never happened.', the same reasoning as migration.md:37, and it sits outside C-16's allowlist as the clause says. Un-named hits the sweep also returns: journal.template.md:23, patterns-journal.template.md:122 and :134, migration.md:31 (the migrator's `last_confirmed` table row, adjacent to the named :37), retrieval-funnel.md:102, and the six `assets/records/*.template.md:8-10` template lines.

findings.description: At 530 lines and 7,368 words the document has passed the point where a reader holds it whole, and the C-3/C-5 contradiction above is the concrete cost rather than a hypothetical one: two blocker clauses forty lines apart, neither cross-referencing the other, disagreeing about what a run does to one record. Both were revised in r2 and neither revision looked at the other.
findings.evidence: `wc -l -w -c .agent-guild/state/constitution.md` -> 530 lines, 7368 words, 50923 bytes. C-3 spans :110-129 and C-5 spans :155-192; C-5's r2 note at :157 says it 'now spans the whole run rather than a single `--note` group' without touching C-3, and C-3 was not revised in r2 at all. The r2 preamble at :14 lists what the batch redesign changes — dedupe scope, order independence, C-17's placement — and does not list monotonicity, which is the one it silently changed the meaning of.

findings.description: The structural half of the r1 blocker is genuinely closed, and closed at the level the spec states rather than papered over. Batch scope makes invocation scope and run scope the same thing, so 'confirmed twice in one run is stamped once' becomes a property of the script instead of a property of how the caller loops. The realpath trap r0 found still bites, and the corrected check discriminates all three sub-cases.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:42 'It is called once per run, not once per input... That is what makes the issue's "a record confirmed twice in one run is stamped once" a property of the script rather than a property of how the caller happens to loop.' Confirmed the realpath trap still holds at 924f81f: `mktemp -d` returns /var/folders/2b/.../T/tmp.XXXX whose real path is /private/var/folders/..., so C-5 case 3 separates a string-equality dedupe from a realpath one. With the mutation corrected, the check returns `grep -c` = 1 for both sub-checks, `order-independent`, `stamped: 1  skipped: 0`, and the record at 2026-02-17 — the later of the two group dates, not the last processed.

findings.description: Runs clean against a conforming batch-scoped stamper, and the r1 SCRIPT-CONTRACT minor is closed: `--dry-run` and the closing count are both exercised, and all three malformed invocations are pinned including the `--note` case that made r1's C-6 doubly unattributable.
findings.evidence: Ran the check verbatim against the reference stamper: 'dry-run wrote nothing', 'dry and wet output identical', `stamped: _memory/context/atlas-region-topology-mPmy8XBe5H.md 2026-02-10 -> 2026-02-17`, `stamped: 1  skipped: 0`, `exit=0`, `last_confirmed: 2026-02-17`, then `no such record: ...` / `bad-record exit=2`, `no such note: ...` / `bad-note exit=2`, `record path before any --note: ...` / `no-group exit=2`. Only wrinkle in the text: :64 says all three cases 'name the path that failed', and the no-group case has no path — the check's own wording at :84 ('name what failed') is the right one.

findings.description: Unchanged and still the sharpest of the script clauses. The batch redesign strengthens it rather than weakening it: the v1 record and the v2 record now go in as one group in one invocation, which is the mixed case AC7 actually cares about.
findings.evidence: Ran the check verbatim against the reference stamper: `skipped: _memory/decisions/freeze-window-owned-by-ops-ocPwdpeY0a.md (v1 record, no schema key)`, `stamped: _memory/context/atlas-region-topology-mPmy8XBe5H.md 2026-02-10 -> 2026-02-17`, `stamped: 1  skipped: 1`, `exit=0`, `v1 untouched`. The fixture still has the shape the clause needs: no `schema` key, `status: accepted`, no `last_confirmed`.

findings.description: Runs clean, and its python mutation is the correct read-then-write form the two broken clauses should copy — it reads into `t` on its own line before truncating.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:139-142 `t = open(p).read()` then `open(p, "w").write(t.replace(...))`. Ran the check verbatim against the reference stamper: `skipped: ... (status: proposed, not accepted)`, `stamped: 0  skipped: 1`, `exit=0`, `held`. The `count=1` confines the replacement to the copied record's own `status` line.

findings.description: Runs clean against the batch call, and the batch redesign makes it stronger: passing the v2 and v1 records together in one invocation means the `diff -r` now proves the run touched exactly one file out of two it was handed.
findings.evidence: Ran the check verbatim against the reference stamper: `diff -r` output was one file and one line pair, `8c8 < last_confirmed: 2026-02-10 --- > last_confirmed: 2026-02-17`, and `before=failures: 0 after=failures: 0`.

findings.description: Unchanged from r1 and unaffected by batch scope, since it explicitly hands placement to C-17. Four independently checkable propositions plus a concrete structural failure mode.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:300-301. The budget sentence it cites is verbatim at SKILL.md:67 '**Five body reads per input, and the budget binds.**' and the accepted-only rule it says it matches is at SKILL.md:69 'Only `status: accepted` records produce flags.' Phase 2.5's per-input loop opens at SKILL.md:59.

findings.description: Unchanged from r1 and still resolved against C-14. Batch scope does not disturb it: the stamper's skip list is now one list per run rather than one per input, which is if anything easier for phase 6 to render faithfully.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:307 'every record the **stamper** declined to write ... Records merely read at phase 2.5 and not judged confirmed are outside this list'; the rubric at :308 asks the checker to confirm that scoping. Reconciles with C-14's fourth fixture record (constitution.md:439), which is graded as an absence of stamp rather than as a required report line.

findings.description: Unchanged and still the sharpest rubric in the document. The two-exceptions contradiction test is anchored to a line that really exists and really closes the Operating Rules list.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:459 '**VTT raw content is collapsed, not verbatim.** ... This is the one sanctioned exception to preserving raw content exactly as captured.' The Operating Rules heading is at SKILL.md:450 and the list ends at :459.

findings.description: The r1 minor is closed the right way. The document-level obligation on `assets/claude-md/_memory.template.md` keeps the `:65` pre-ruling from emptying the file of any mention, and it is stated as a burden on the document rather than on a sentence, so the two rulings no longer pull against each other. The floor moved from ten to twelve and both additions are the ones r1's re-derivation surfaced.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:326 'accounts for the write-through *somewhere in the document* ... that pre-ruling is about the sentence, not about the file, and the file still owes the reader an account.' Verified the premise: _memory.template.md:21 is `last_confirmed: YYYY-MM-DD` inside the required-frontmatter block at :15-23, with no account anywhere in the file of how the value is set; 'How Records Get Created' at :60-74 is about creation only. The floor's two new entries resolve: :21 and references/retrieval-funnel.md:40 ('# last_confirmed at all, so they are absent from this result rather than stale').

findings.description: The r1 minor is closed and closed better than C-16's version of the same fix. Pinning the literal base SHA rather than `HEAD` means C-12 survives a commit outright — `git show <base>:<file>` against the working-tree file compares the same two things whether or not the worker committed — so the clause is not merely warned about vacuity, it is immune to it.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:357 `BASE=924f81f7d4c9794968a2954f8152dc6ed53cc9df`. Ran the check verbatim: no diff, `inventory exit=0`. All four enumerating files are in the loop including SKILL.md, which was the r0 hole. One overstatement to note, cosmetic: C-16's failure string at :481 says 'HEAD MOVED — THIS CHECK AND C-12 ARE BOTH VACUOUS', but C-12 is precisely the one that is not.

findings.description: All three r1 defects are closed. The placement check is bounded on both sides and anchored on code the clause does not instruct the worker to reword; the restore assertion is a shasum comparison that can actually fail against an untracked file; and the fixture-damage check closes the tree-damage gap r1 flagged alongside it.
findings.evidence: Both anchors resolve exactly as the constitution says: `grep -n 'fixtures_before=' | head -1` -> 586, `grep -n '"\$fixtures_before"' | tail -1` -> 1299 (a single hit, so head/tail cannot drift). Ran the placement block verbatim at 924f81f: `snap=586 first= last= cmp=1299`, `OUTSIDE THE GUARD` — it fails safe on zero hits rather than passing on empty strings. The restore step takes `orig` after copying the real script aside and before overwriting (constitution.md:399), so the comparison at :425 has a real fixed point; `/bin/cat >` truncates in place and preserves the mode, so `cp` back restores byte-for-byte. Guard semantics confirmed: snapshot at :586 over `tests/fixtures/inbox-to-memory`, comparison at :1299, file ends at :1309.

findings.description: Unchanged, still runs, still returns exactly the one hit the clause predicts, and the interaction with C-13 is coherent: the new section lands between :586 and :1299 and therefore pushes the never-migrate rule further down, which is why the clause asks for a greppable form rather than a renumbered one.
findings.evidence: Ran the sweep verbatim: one hit, `_maintenance//inbox-to-memory/eval-scope.sh:6:inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:1226`. The rule it cites lives at tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:1296-1298, so the citation is already wrong today. eval-scope.sh:3-6 is the comment carrying it.

findings.description: The r1 minor is closed: the `HEAD` assertion catches the commit-first hole that made `check-diff-scope.py` pass against an empty diff. The allowlist is otherwise unchanged and still correct, and the new eval fixture does not disturb the smoke suite, which names its fixture scopes individually rather than enumerating the directory.
findings.evidence: Ran the check verbatim: three suites exit 0, `HEAD is the base`, `OK: 0 path(s) in scope`, `scope exit=0`. `git rev-parse HEAD` = 924f81f7d4c9794968a2954f8152dc6ed53cc9df, `git status --porcelain` empty. tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:109-117 requires `$fixtures/old-only`, `$fixtures/mixed`, `$fixtures/broken` by name and greps nothing for `evals`, so a fifth eval fixture cannot redden the suite. lint-scope.sh stays out of the allowlist, so the second lock on the no-lint-changes non-goal holds.

findings.description: All seven acceptance criteria map to clauses that would catch their violation, AC6 included — the r1 blocker is structurally closed. AC1 -> C-1, C-6, C-8, C-13, C-17. AC2 -> C-2, C-13 (with the saboteur now making the assertion falsifiable). AC3 -> C-9. AC4 -> C-8 ('the resulting stamp does not pass through phase 5'), C-17 ('before phase 5'), the contract's 'It writes by default. No --apply', and C-14's no-per-record-prompt row. AC5 -> C-10. AC6 -> the batch contract at :42 plus C-5 case 2 plus C-13's required cross-group assertion; because one run is now one invocation, C-5's invocation scope and the spec's run scope are the same scope.
